## Authentication standards and guidance

What do the standards say about proving who someone is?

| Resource | Run by | What it is and when to use it | Kind | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [NIST SP 800-63 Digital Identity Guidelines](https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/) | NIST | Revision 4 as web pages: a base volume and volumes on identity proofing and enrollment, authenticators and their management, and federation and assertions. | Standard | Free |
| [FIDO User Authentication Specifications](https://fidoalliance.org/specifications/) | FIDO Alliance | Overview of the authentication specifications by family: FIDO2, with W3C WebAuthn and the CTAP1 and CTAP2 protocols, FIDO UAF, and FIDO U2F, linking the downloads. | Standard | Free |
| [passkeys.dev](https://passkeys.dev/) | Members of the W3C Web Identity & Credentials Adoption CG and the FIDO Alliance | Developer site for passkeys with documentation, a device support page, and tools including a WebAuthn response decoder. | Reference | Free |
| [Passkey Central](https://www.passkeycentral.org/home) | FIDO Alliance | Guidance for organizations adopting passkeys: an introduction, the business case, rollout planning, user journey design, and launch, with sections on workforce sign-ins and resources. | Reference | Free |
| [Guide to Web Authentication](https://webauthn.guide/) | Duo Security | Illustrated walk through Web Authentication: why passwords fail, how public key credentials work, and the browser API calls for registering and authenticating, with annotated code. | Reference | Free |
| [RFC 9700: Best Current Practice for OAuth 2.0 Security](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9700/) | IETF | Security recommendations for OAuth 2.0 deployments, including redirect-based flows, token replay, access token privilege, and client authentication, with an updated attacker model and attack mitigations. | Standard | Free |
| [RFC 8725: JSON Web Token Best Current Practices](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc8725/) | IETF | Catalogs attacks on JSON Web Tokens, including weak signatures, weak symmetric keys, and substitution, then practices against them, such as algorithm verification and audience validation. | Standard | Free |
| [Authentication Cheat Sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authentication_Cheat_Sheet.html) | OWASP Foundation | Developer guidance on topics including user IDs, password strength and recovery, re-authentication, error messages, automated attack defenses, logging, and protocols that need no password. | Reference | Free |
| [How OpenID Connect Works](https://openid.net/developers/how-connect-works/) | OpenID Foundation | The OpenID Foundation's explanation of OpenID Connect, the authentication protocol built on OAuth 2.0. | Standard | Free |
| [OAuth 2.0](https://oauth.net/2/) | Aaron Parecki | Guide to OAuth 2.0, the protocol for authorization. | Standard | Free |
| [FIDO Passkeys](https://fidoalliance.org/passkeys/) | FIDO Alliance | The FIDO Alliance's explanation of passkeys, the FIDO credential that signs a user in with the device's own unlock method. | Standard | Free |

Listed here from another domain: How OpenID Connect Works ([Identity and directory services administration](identity-and-directory-administration.md#protocols-and-standards)), OAuth 2.0 ([Identity and directory services administration](identity-and-directory-administration.md#protocols-and-standards)), FIDO Passkeys ([Identity and directory services administration](identity-and-directory-administration.md#protocols-and-standards)).

## Active Directory and Entra defense

How do I find and close the paths to domain admin?

| Resource | Run by | What it is and when to use it | Kind | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Active Directory & Azure AD/Entra ID Security](https://adsecurity.org/) | Sean Metcalf | Posts on securing Active Directory and Entra ID, including a fundamentals series on Group Policy permissions, AdminSDHolder, and domain controller security, and numbered security tips. *Last updated on May 19, 2026.* | Research blog | Free |
| [Purple Knight](https://www.semperis.com/purple-knight/) | Semperis | Semperis's assessment tool for Active Directory, Okta, and Entra ID, with pages on its security indicators, an FAQ, and videos; download needs a request form. | Tool | Free with account |
| [Best practices for securing Active Directory](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/ad-ds/plan/security-best-practices/best-practices-for-securing-active-directory) | Microsoft | Covers how Active Directory gets compromised, then reducing its attack surface, limiting privileges, secure administrative hosts, domain controller protection, monitoring, and planning for compromise. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [Microsoft Entra security operations guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/architecture/security-operations-introduction) | Microsoft | Opens Microsoft's monitoring and alerting guidance for Entra: the data sources to collect, domain controllers included, and strategies by area, including user and privileged accounts. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [Locksmith](https://github.com/jakehildreth/Locksmith) | Jake Hildreth (jakehildreth) | PowerShell module that scans Active Directory Certificate Services for misconfigurations and, depending on the mode, prints them, writes them to CSV, or applies the fixes. | Tool | Free |
| [Attack and Defense Playbook for Microsoft Entra](https://github.com/Cloud-Architekt/AzureAD-Attack-Defense) | Thomas Naunheim (Cloud-Architekt) | Chapters on attacks against Entra ID, including password spray, consent grants, token replay, and adversary-in-the-middle, with detection rule templates and a MITRE ATT&CK mapping. | Reference | Free |
| [Maester](https://maester.dev/) | Maester Team | PowerShell test framework for Microsoft 365 tenants whose checks follow published baselines and can be extended with packs; the Maester Cloud edition is paid. | Tool | Freemium |
| [Adalanche](https://github.com/lkarlslund/Adalanche) | Lars Karlslund (lkarlslund) | Graphs ownership, ACLs, and other relationships between Active Directory objects to show who can take control of what; some features are in the paid version. | Tool | Freemium |
| [Active Directory Security Assessment Checklist](https://cert.cyber.gouv.fr/uploads/ad_checklist.html) | ANSSI | Graded list of Active Directory weaknesses for scoring a forest, with descriptions, recommended measures, and a changelog; French, with an English toggle. | Reference | Free |
| [BloodHound Community Edition](https://github.com/SpecterOps/BloodHound) | SpecterOps | Graphs the privilege relationships in Active Directory, Azure, and other identity platforms so that attack paths stand out; this is the open source Community Edition. | Tool | Free |
| [PingCastle](https://www.pingcastle.com/) | Netwrix | Scores an Active Directory or Entra ID environment against a maturity model and reports risk indicators; free to download, with paid editions. | Tool | Freemium |

Listed here from another domain: BloodHound Community Edition ([Offensive security](offensive-security.md#active-directory-and-windows)), PingCastle ([Offensive security](offensive-security.md#active-directory-and-windows)).

## Zero trust and privileged access

How do I limit what a stolen account can reach?

| Resource | Run by | What it is and when to use it | Kind | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Zero trust architecture design principles](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/collection/zero-trust/architecture-design-principles) | NCSC, a part of GCHQ | Principles for building a zero trust network, from knowing your architecture and identities through policy-based authorization and monitoring to trusting no network, your own included. | Reference | Free |
| [Zero Trust Guidance Center](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/zero-trust/) | Microsoft | Hub that routes to Microsoft's zero trust guidance by technology pillar, business scenario, or security discipline, with links to training and assessment tools. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [Securing privileged access](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/privileged-access-workstations/overview) | Microsoft | Overview of Microsoft's privileged access strategy, with a rapid modernization plan for quick wins, best practices, and industry references including NCSC, ACSC, and MITRE ATT&CK. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [NIST SP 800-207](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/207/final) | NIST | Defines zero trust tenets and the logical components of an architecture, then deployment scenarios, threats, links to federal guidance, and migrating a perimeter-based network. | Standard | Free |

## Passwords and secrets

How should passwords, passkeys, and secrets be chosen and stored?

| Resource | Run by | What it is and when to use it | Kind | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Pwned Passwords](https://haveibeenpwned.com/Passwords) | Have I Been Pwned (Superlative Enterprises Pty Ltd) | Checks whether a password appears in known breaches, by web form, by an API built on k-anonymity, or offline with the open source downloader. | Online service | Free |
| [Password administration for system owners](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/collection/passwords) | NCSC, a part of GCHQ | Collection for those who set password policy: how to update a policy's approach and a buyers guide for password managers, with an infographic to download. | Reference | Free |
| [EFF Dice-Generated Passphrases](https://www.eff.org/dice) | Electronic Frontier Foundation | Directions for rolling dice against EFF's long wordlist to build a passphrase, with notes on when to use one and on the different wordlists. | Reference | Free |
| [KeePassXC](https://keepassxc.org/) | KeePassXC Team | Password manager for Windows, macOS, and Linux that keeps entries in an encrypted file you store yourself and auto-fills them into other applications. | Tool | Free |
| [Bitwarden](https://bitwarden.com/) | Bitwarden, Inc. | Password manager with a free personal account; paid plans add sharing and event logs for teams, and single sign-on, policies, and self-hosting for enterprises. | Online service | Freemium |
| [Password Storage Cheat Sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Password_Storage_Cheat_Sheet.html) | OWASP Foundation | Covers stored-password protection, including hashing versus encryption, salting, peppering, work factors, the choice among Argon2id, scrypt, bcrypt, and PBKDF2, and upgrading legacy hashes. | Reference | Free |
| [Secrets Management Cheat Sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Secrets_Management_Cheat_Sheet.html) | OWASP Foundation | General practices for managing secrets, then sections on CI/CD pipelines, cloud providers, containers and orchestrators, implementation, encryption, detection, and incident response. | Reference | Free |
| [Gitleaks](https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks) | Gitleaks | Command-line scanner for hard-coded secrets in git repositories, directories and files, or standard input, with a pre-commit hook, baselines for known findings, and configurable rules. *In maintenance mode.* | Tool | Free |
| [TruffleHog](https://github.com/trufflesecurity/trufflehog) | Truffle Security | Scans places including Git, logs, object stores, and filesystems for credentials, classifies them, and can report only verified ones; the enterprise edition is paid. | Tool | Freemium |
| [SOPS: Secrets OPerationS](https://getsops.io/) | SOPS Authors | Encrypts values in YAML, JSON, INI, and dotenv files while leaving keys readable, with identities including age, PGP, cloud key management services, and HashiCorp Vault. | Tool | Free |

## Cryptography and PKI

Which algorithms, key sizes, and certificate practices are sound?

| Resource | Run by | What it is and when to use it | Kind | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Cryptographic Standards and Guidelines](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/cryptographic-standards-and-guidelines) | NIST | NIST's index of its cryptography work by area, including block cipher techniques, digital signatures, hash functions, key management, post-quantum cryptography, and random bit generation. | Reference | Free |
| [Post-Quantum Cryptography](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/post-quantum-cryptography) | NIST | Project page for NIST's post-quantum standards: FIPS 203, 204, and 205 (ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA), with sections on migration and continuing standardization. | Reference | Free |
| [Cryptographic Module Validation Program](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/cryptographic-module-validation-program) | NIST and the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security | Home of the joint US and Canadian program that validates cryptographic modules against FIPS 140, with the rules on using FIPS 140-2 and 140-3 modules. | Reference | Free |
| [Baseline Requirements](https://cabforum.org/working-groups/server/baseline-requirements/) | CA/Browser Forum | Requirements that TLS server certificates must meet, with links including current and past versions, a conversion table to the RFC 3647 format, and an FAQ. | Standard | Free |
| [Certificate Transparency](https://certificate.transparency.dev/) | Google | Explains why certificate authorities need watching and how append-only logs expose what they issue, with pages on logs, monitors, and user agents. | Reference | Free |
| [RFC 9846: The Transport Layer Security (TLS) Protocol Version 1.3](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9846/) | IETF | The TLS 1.3 specification that replaces RFC 8446, including the protocol overview, presentation language, handshake and record protocols, anti-replay mechanisms, and compliance requirements. | Standard | Free |
| [badkeys](https://badkeys.info/) | Hanno Böck | Paste a certificate, signing request, or key to test it for known weaknesses, including ROCA, Fermat factorization, and Debian OpenSSL weak keys. | Online service | Free |
| [age](https://github.com/FiloSottile/age) | Filippo Valsorda (FiloSottile) | Command-line file encryption and a Go library: encrypt to several recipients, a passphrase, or SSH keys, with post-quantum keys and inspection of encrypted files. | Tool | Free |
| [The GNU Privacy Guard](https://gnupg.org/) | The GnuPG Project | Home of the OpenPGP implementation GnuPG: release announcements and security advisories for it, Libgcrypt, and Gpg4win, plus downloads, manuals, and guides. | Tool | Free |
| [The Sodium crypto library (libsodium)](https://libsodium.gitbook.io/doc) | Frank Denis (jedisct1) | Manual for libsodium: installation and a quickstart, then chapters by task, including public-key and secret-key cryptography, password hashing, key exchange, and key derivation. | Vendor documentation | Free |
| [The Cryptopals Crypto Challenges](https://cryptopals.com/) | Cryptography Services, NCC Group | Sets of programming exercises that have you break cryptography, from basics and block ciphers through stream ciphers, Diffie-Hellman, RSA, DSA, and hashes to abstract algebra. | Training or lab | Free |
| [TLSRef Docs](https://docs.tlsref.org/) (formerly Security/Server Side TLS on MozillaWiki) | TLSRef | Community-run successor to Mozilla's server-side TLS guidelines: recommended settings for the Modern and Intermediate profiles and a cross-reference of cipher suite names between TLS libraries. | Reference | Free |
| [TLS Configurator](https://configurator.tlsref.org/) (formerly Mozilla SSL Configuration Generator) | TLSRef | Pick server software such as Apache, nginx, HAProxy, or Postfix, a profile, and the server and OpenSSL versions, and it writes a matching TLS configuration. | Online service | Free |
| [NIST SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev. 5](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/57/pt1/r5/final) | NIST | Key management guidance including key types and usage, cryptoperiods, algorithm and key-size selection, protection requirements, key states and transitions, and phases from pre-operational to destroyed. | Standard | Free |
| [crt.sh](https://crt.sh/) | Sectigo | Searches Certificate Transparency logs: look up a domain or organization to list the certificates logged for it; run by Sectigo. | Online service | Free |

Listed here from another domain: crt.sh ([Threat intelligence and adversaries](threat-intelligence.md#internet-scan-and-exposure-data)).

## Data protection and privacy

How do I classify, encrypt, and dispose of data?

| Resource | Run by | What it is and when to use it | Kind | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [NIST Privacy Framework](https://www.nist.gov/privacy-framework) | NIST | Home of the framework, including the version 1.1 public draft, its mapping from version 1.0, a learning center, quick start guide, and resource repository. | Standard | Free |
| [Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj) | Publications Office of the European Union | Official Journal text of the EU's data protection regulation in the Union's languages as HTML and PDF, with links to consolidated versions and a summary. | Reference | Free |
| [California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA)](https://oag.ca.gov/privacy/ccpa) | State of California Department of Justice, Office of the Attorney General | Questions and answers by topic, including the opt-out from sale or sharing, requests to know, delete, and correct, required notices, and data brokers. | Reference | Free |
| [VeraCrypt](https://veracrypt.io/en/Home.html) | AM Crypto | Disk encryption for Windows, macOS, and Linux, including file containers mounted as drives, partitions or devices, Windows system drive with pre-boot authentication, and hidden volumes. | Tool | Free |
| [Cryptomator](https://cryptomator.org/) | Skymatic GmbH | Encrypts files on your device before they reach cloud storage, in vaults unlocked by password; desktop is free, mobile and team editions are paid. | Tool | Freemium |
| [nwipe](https://github.com/martijnvanbrummelen/nwipe) | Martijn van Brummelen (martijnvanbrummelen) | Linux disk eraser with a choice of overwrite methods and random number generators, ATA and NVMe secure erase, and instructions for a bootable USB version. | Tool | Free |
| [Privacy Guides](https://www.privacyguides.org/en/) | Privacy Guides | Volunteer-run site with a knowledge base that includes threat modeling, tool and service recommendations by category, news, and a forum. | Reference | Free |
| [NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/88/r2/final) | NIST | Describes sanitization methods including cryptographic erase, then a sanitization program, including policy, scope, a decision framework, assurance, and documentation, with a sample certificate. | Standard | Free |
| [cryptsetup](https://gitlab.com/cryptsetup/cryptsetup) | cryptsetup | Source repository for the Linux disk encryption utility and LUKS format, linking LUKS1 and LUKS2 specifications, release notes, an FAQ, and build requirements by distribution. | Tool | Free |
| [UK GDPR guidance and resources](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/uk-gdpr-guidance-and-resources/) | ICO | ICO guidance on UK data protection by topic, including subject access requests, lawful basis, controllers and processors, international transfers, security, data sharing, and children's information. | Reference | Free |
| [Microsoft Purview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/) | Microsoft | Microsoft's documentation hub for Purview, split into its governance, security, and compliance solutions, with setup guides for each. | Vendor documentation | Free |
